transcript: Becky Shaw is the kind of play that'll make you laugh, gasp, and question, who is in the right here? And then realise the answer is maybe no one. And that's what makes it so compelling. Becky Shaw starts with a simple premise. Newly wed set up. Two people on a blind date who should definitely never have been set up. And from there, everything spirals. Relationships start to crack, secrets come out, and one bad night turns to consequences that ripple through everyone's lives. There are only five characters in Becky Shaw, but a seemingly unlimited amount of complicated dynamics. And there's also this question that kind of runs through the entire show. What does it actually mean to be a good person? Is it kinder to tell the truth even when it hurts, or to lie to spare someone's feelings? But it's funny because while they are arguing about this in the play, no one is choosing the nice option. Everyone is as honest and brutal as they can possibly be. And it's shocking, but it's also kind of refreshing. It all just works so well because of this incredible cast. Our show had a talk back afterwards, and it was so cool getting to listen to the insights of this cast and creative team. Patrick Ball, Madeline Brewer and Alden Enriq are all making their Broadway debuts, and I love all of them from T V. And movies, so it's just great getting to see them on Stage. And then, of course, Lauren Patten, who, to me, like, carries the heart of the show. Her character, Susanna, makes the wrong choice, like, every single time. But because Lauren Patten is so good, you just root for her as this incredible, complex and a toxic relationship with her mom. Played by Linda Emond, who is so funny and gets all of the best one liners. Anyway, Becky Shaw is playing right now at the Hayes Theater. You're not gonna Wanna miss this one.
